items.text:
Modern  attention  has  become  a  fragile  currency,  scattered across endless notifications and competing demands. To regain a  sense  of  inward  steadiness,  one  must  first  recognise  that focus is not a sudden achievement but a gradual discipline. It is (51)____through  deliberate  pauses,  through  the  willingness  to step  back  from  constant  stimulation.  True  attention  is  less about  tightening  one's  grip  and  more about noticing what truly deserves to be held.
In a culture that rewards speed, slowness is often dismissed as inefficiency,  yet slowness is the very soil in which depth grows. Without  intervals  of  quiet,  the  mind  becomes  a  surface  skim, unable  to  draw  meaning  from  its  own  patterns.  To  cultivate sustained attention, individuals must learn to create spaces free from  interruption,  spaces  in which thought can wander without being instantly (52)_____.

items.text:
The challenge is not merely to avoid distraction but to understand why distraction feels so seductive. It offers effortless  escape  from  complexity.  But  genuine  engagement requires a willingness to remain in the discomfort of uncertainty. Focus  strengthens  when  we practise returning again and again to  the  task  at  hand, where each return becomes a silent act of (53)_____.
Over time, attention reveals its own architecture. It teaches that clarity emerges not from force but from consistency. It teaches, too, that the mind cannot be  endlessly  stretched  without consequence;  it  needs  rest  just  as  much  as  effort.  To reclaim our  capacity  for  deep  noticing,  we  must  replace  the  habit  of constant  reaction  with  the  habit  of  (54)____.  Only  then  does perception regain its depth, and thought its quiet authority.
Ultimately,  attention  is not a resource to be squeezed dry but a relationship to be honoured. And like any meaningful relationship, it flourishes when we protect it from the noise that seeks to (55)_____ it.

- Q.51. (a) harvested
- (b) demanded
- (c) cultivated

items.text:
Economic stability is often described through charts and targets, yet its foundations reach far deeper than numerical summaries. A nation's economy depends not only on policies and production but also on the confidence held by households and firms. When
people believe conditions are favourable, they are more likely to spend, invest, and innovate. Such confidence cannot be (56)_____through declarations alone; it grows through consistent governance and transparent communication.
Periods  of  uncertainty  reveal  how  quickly  expectations  shape behaviour. Even minor doubts can alter consumption  and investment decisions. Economists refer to this as the 'expectations  effect,'  noting  that  markets  react  as  strongly  to perception  as  they  do  to  measurable  data.  When expectations turn pessimistic, caution  may  (57)____  growth  long  before official indicators reflect the shift.
Public policy therefore carries a psychological dimension. Reforms must not only be effective but must also inspire trust. Policies  that  appear  inconsistent  or  disconnected  from  daily realities breed scepticism. In contrast, clarity and steady execution help create a sense of direction that (58)___ economic resilience.

items.text:
Another challenge lies in  balancing  immediate  needs  with long-term  goals.  Measures  aimed  at  short-term  stability  can sometimes compete with investments required for future development. Without careful balance, economies risk becoming reactive,  thereby  (59)_____  their  capacity to adapt to changing global circumstances.
Ultimately,  stability  does  not mean the absence of volatility but the  strength  to  withstand  it.  When institutions function reliably and trust is nurtured, societies can face uncertainty with greater confidence, transforming temporary disruptions into opportunities for renewed (60)_____.

Astronomy  reminds  us  that  humanity  occupies  only  a  small corner of an immense cosmic landscape. For centuries, observers  have  studied  the  night sky to understand not merely its beauty but the forces that govern celestial motion. Knowledge  of  the  universe  advances  when  evidence  replaces speculation and when observations are (61)____with disciplined curiosity rather than hurried assumptions.
One  of the most profound shifts in astronomical thinking came with the recognition that the universe is not static. Galaxies drift apart, stars evolve, and cosmic structures continually transform. Such  discoveries  emerge  slowly,  shaped  by  measurements  so
delicate that even minor errors can (62)_____ an entire model. Astronomers  also  rely  on  patterns  of  light  to  infer  distant realities.  A  star's  temperature,  age,  and  composition  can  be examined  through  its  spectrum,  offering  clues  that  human senses  alone  could  never  detect.  This  method  demonstrates how scientific insight often comes from interpreting signals that are easily (63)_____without careful study.
In recent years, the search for planets beyond our solar system
